answer: A seat is a mining claim, not a login. Each applicant stakes a distinct surveyed block on the open meadow, has a licensed assayer core it and record the umber seam's signature, and lodges the core in a bonded shed; two seats on one block collide on the survey. Assessment work follows a spiral: the first claim owes one week of labor on site, the fifth owes sixteen, and each further block doubles the toll, so holding k blocks demands 2 to the k weeks of unshareable fieldwork. A farm must buy ground, drill, assay and store each block alone; an honest claimer works a week for clear title.
